newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Drnovsek likely to win new term as PM.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Drnovsek likely to win new term as PM.

text.p: Attempts by Slovenia's acting centre-left prime minister Janez Drnovsek to form a new government took a dramatic turn on Wednesday when he apparently won backing from a rightwinger who defected from his party.

Drnovsek, who led Slovenia's government for four of the five years since independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, appeared to have little chance of winning of a majority in a parliamentary vote, which had been due at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT).
The vote was postponed until 12.30 p.m. (1130 GMT) after Christian Democrat Ciril Pucko announced he was defecting from his party to sit in parliament as an independent.

"Pucko has decided to support Drnovsek's candidacy (for prime minister). He has left the Christian Democrats," the leader of Drnovsek's Liberal Democrat parliamentary group, Tone Anderlic, told Reuters.
Parliamentary speaker Janez Podobnik confirmed that Pucko had defected and said he had postponed the parliamentary vote.

Drnovsek, whose Liberal Democrats won 25 of 90 parliamentary seats in a November 10 general election, had already secured the votes of a further 20 deputies from smaller parties in parliament, including former communists.
But the one extra vote needed for an absolute majority had eluded him until Wednesday's surprise defection.
If Pucko does vote for Drnovsek's candidacy for prime minister, it will put paid to the chances of an alliance of three rightwing parties to deprive Drnovsek of a second term in government.
The alliance, comprising the conservative People's Party, the centre-right Social Democrats and the Christian Democrats, had remained united since the election.
The right had been pressing for People's Party leader Marjan Podobnik, 36, to be called to form the next government if Drnovsek lost the parliamentary vote.
